outcomes.text: Learn the knowledge needed to analyse performance texts and live theatre in the written exam.
Identify genre, structure, form and style of a play.
Analyse character, motivation, interaction, language and sub-text.
Explain how mood, atmosphere, pace, rhythm and climax are created.
Use stage directions and weigh the practical demands of a text.
Place a play in its social, cultural and historical context.
Describe the theatrical conventions of the period a play was written in.
Explain how performance conventions, space and actor-audience layout convey meaning.
Explain design fundamentals: scale, shape, colour and texture.
Describe set and prop design, including revolves, trucks, projection and flying.
Describe costume, hair and make-up design.
Describe lighting design: direction, colour, intensity and effects.
Describe sound design: direction, amplification, music and effects.
Analyse vocal interpretation: accent, pitch, pace, intonation and delivery.
Analyse physical interpretation: movement, posture, gesture and expression.
Use stage positions: upstage, downstage, centre and left or right.
Name staging types: in the round, proscenium arch, thrust, traverse, end on and promenade.
Explain how each staging configuration affects use of space.
Describe the roles of playwright, performer, understudy, designers, technician, director and managers.
Explain what each role does day to day and what each is accountable for.
Study and explore practically one set play from the list, such as The Crucible or Blood Brothers.
Understand the characteristics and context of the whole play.
Explore practical ideas for interpreting the play.
Link design to context and theatrical conventions.

topics.title: 3.1.3 Area of study 2 - Live theatre production

outcomes.text: Analyse and evaluate the work of live theatre performers and designers.
Explain how the production interpreted the play and what messages it communicated.
Judge how well performers and designers communicated meaning.
Research the plot, characters, style and context of the production seen.
Choose one specialism: performer, or lighting, sound, set, costume or puppet designer.
Create and develop ideas to communicate meaning in devised theatre.
Research, develop ideas and collaborate with others.
Rehearse, refine and amend work in progress.
Analyse and evaluate your own devising process.
Contribute as performer or designer to a devised piece for an audience.
Create and communicate meaning and realise artistic intention.
Choose a specialism and contribute to text-based drama for an audience.
Interpret texts, communicate meaning and realise artistic intention in two extracts.
Develop the skills of your chosen specialism.
Learn lines and create a character suited to the performance.
Develop vocal skills: diction, intonation, pace, projection and emotional range.
Develop physical skills: movement, posture, gesture, stillness and spatial awareness.
Keep a performer-audience relationship and work safely.
Design lighting that sets location, time and mood and conveys meaning.
Create effects with colour, gobos, filters, fades, blackouts and shadow.
Choose and position lanterns, and rig, angle and focus them safely.
Design sound that sets location, period and mood and conveys meaning.
Select equipment such as microphones, amplifiers and software.
Use live and recorded sound, directional sound, music and effects such as reverb, fades and soundscapes.
Design sets that set location, period and mood and convey meaning.
Choose materials such as flats, cyclorama, drapes and projections.
Plan for stage configuration, entrances, scene changes, space, scale and levels, and select dressings and props.
Design costumes that show character, period, location and mood.
Choose fabrics, textures and accessories and attend to colour, shape, fit and movement.
Design make-up and hair appropriate to character, age and period.
Design a puppet with clear character and audience appeal.
Choose construction materials, colour, texture and costume.
Consider structure, scale, performer manipulation and puppet types such as rod, string and shadow.
